description: Curated display/body pairings. Same move as the bands: choose from a finite set rather than compose a new combination, because pairing type is a craft skill and the mean answer is recognisable on sight.
why: Asked to pick fonts, a model reaches for the handful it has seen most: Inter with Inter, Poppins with Poppins, a geometric sans with itself at two weights. None of those is wrong, and all of them are why generated pages look related to each other. A pairing is also the cheapest large change available — swapping the pair transforms a page far more than any token in DESIGN.md, at no structural cost.
how_to_use: Pick one entry, then write its `display` and `body` into DESIGN.md's typography tokens verbatim. The scale, weights and sizes still come from the type contrast band — a pairing decides which families, never how big.

editorial-serif.feel: Warm, bookish, opinionated. A soft serif with real optical sizing against a neutral workhorse.
editorial-serif.suits: Consumer products with a human story, D2C, anything that wants to feel made rather than shipped.

swiss.feel: Neutral, dense, engineered. One family at two optical widths; the hierarchy comes from scale, not contrast.
swiss.suits: Developer tools, infrastructure, dashboards — anywhere the content is the argument and the type should get out of the way.

brutal.feel: Loud, flat, confident. Very heavy display against a plain companion.
brutal.suits: Launches, events, anything that would rather be remembered than trusted.

humanist.feel: High-contrast serif with a calm humanist sans. Traditional, legible, slightly formal.
humanist.suits: Finance, health, education — products where credibility outranks personality.

technical.feel: Quirky geometric display with a workmanlike body. Reads modern without reading generic.
technical.suits: Data products, AI tooling, anything technical that does not want to look like a bank.

monospace-led.feel: Monospace as display voice. Distinctive, and cheap to get wrong at large sizes — check the headline before committing.
monospace-led.suits: Developer-facing products where the audience reads code all day.

rules.one_pairing: Use exactly one pairing. A third family is not a design decision, it is an unresolved one.
rules.no_composing: Do not mix the display of one pairing with the body of another. These are chosen for how the two behave together — the pairing IS the unit, and recombining them puts you back to composing a new one, which is what this file exists to avoid.
rules.substitution: Any pairing may be replaced wholesale with the product's own brand faces when it has them. Licensed brand type always beats a catalogue entry; the catalogue exists for the case where nobody has chosen, which is the case where the mean answer wins by default.
